title: useTransition: Deferred Concurrent Updates & Pending State Flags

progressiveExplaining.eli5: When you click a tab to open a heavy photo gallery, you don't want the current tab to vanish into a blank loading spinner. `useTransition` keeps the old tab visible and interactive on screen while quietly loading the new gallery in the background. Once the gallery is completely ready, it swaps the screens in a single flash.
progressiveExplaining.junior: `useTransition` allows you to defer coordinate state updates that trigger `<Suspense>` boundaries. `const [pending, start] = useTransition();`. When you wrap a state change in `start(() => setTab('photos'))`, Solid keeps the current view on screen instead of falling back to the `<Suspense>` loading spinner, while setting `pending()` to `true` so you can show an inline progress bar.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, Solid Transitions prevent disruptive Suspense fallback flashes during in-app navigation. Unlike React (which uses Virtual DOM time-slicing across concurrent fiber lanes), Solid's reactivity is fine-grained and synchronous. Solid implements transitions by branching resource evaluations: async computations triggered inside `start` register with an isolated transition coordinator. The active DOM remains frozen and interactive until all downstream pending `createResource` promises settle, at which point the DOM commits atomically.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: When `start(fn)` executes, Solid sets an internal `Transition` context on the global reactive runtime. Signal writes execute, but newly triggered `SuspenseContext` boundaries are placed in a 'holding' state rather than flipping to fallback. A global transition counter tracks pending promises. When all promises resolve, the transition finishes, `pending()` flips to `false`, and the new DOM elements replace the old view.

interviewGotchas.question: What is the primary difference between how React and SolidJS implement `useTransition`?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test deep architectural comprehension across competing framework paradigms.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: React implements `useTransition` via **CPU Time-Slicing across Virtual DOM Fibers**: it splits component tree rendering into interruptible 5ms chunks across priority Lanes. SolidJS has no Virtual DOM and renders synchronously; it implements `useTransition` as an **Asynchronous Suspense Coordinator**: it tracks pending `createResource` promises and delays swapping Suspense branches in the real DOM until all background fetches complete.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Do not say that SolidJS time-slices JavaScript execution on the main thread. Solid does not time-slice; it coordinates asynchronous resource boundaries.

interviewGotchas.question: Does `useTransition` hold back non-resource state updates?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks knowledge of transition scope and resource requirements.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: No. If a state update inside `start(() => ...)` does not trigger a pending `createResource` or async Suspense boundary, the update applies immediately and synchronously. `useTransition` only delays UI presentation when asynchronous resources suspend downstream.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Wrapping synchronous state changes (like toggling a boolean that renders a local static component) in `useTransition` will have no deferred effect.
